Last Updated: 2026-07-02
Author: Corbenn Labs

MasterContext_v2
Corbenn Labs Vision

Corbenn Labs is a modular AI operating system designed to build, operate, and eventually automate digital businesses.

The long-term objective is not simply to assist the human, but to progressively reduce repetitive human work while preserving human ownership over strategic decisions and final approval.

The human remains the final decision maker.

AI specialists exist to research, think, create, organize, and execute within clearly defined workflow boundaries.

The operating system evolves through validated iterations rather than assumptions.

Operating Philosophy

Authority Order: When conflicts exist, authority follows this order: 1. SYSTEM_BOOT.md 2. MasterContext_v2.md 3. PROJECT_STATE.md 4. Project-specific documentation 5. Agent outputs. No lower-level document may override a higher-level authority.

Core principles: Evidence over assumptions. Specialization over generalization. Modular architecture. Single Source of Truth. Human approval before public release. Automate repetitive work. Protect workflow boundaries. Continuous improvement.

Corbenn Labs Architecture
Human - Owns: Vision, Final approval, Business ownership. Never delegates final responsibility.

Executive Layer - CEO - Purpose: Direct the operating system. Responsibilities: Define business objectives, Open and close workflow gates, Delegate work, Approve strategic decisions, Maintain alignment with long-term vision.

Intelligence Layer - Researcher - Purpose: Produce evidence. Never creates strategy. Never makes business decisions. Output: Research reports.

Marketing Strategist - Purpose: Transform evidence into business strategy. Produces: Marketing plans, Publishing calendars, Growth strategy, Campaign planning.

Production Layer - Content Engine - Purpose: Convert approved strategy into production plans. Produces: Creative briefs, Content systems, Production packages, Content calendars. Does NOT edit videos. Does NOT publish content.

Support Layer - Executive Briefing Agent, Prompt Architect, Office Manager.

Current Status: Phase 2 - Operational Optimization. Validated Specialists: CEO, Researcher, Marketing Strategist, Content Engine.

Guiding Rule: A new specialist is created only after repetitive human work has been observed enough times to justify automation. Corbenn Labs automates validated work, never hypothetical work.

Governance: MasterContext_v2.md is a protected document. Only the CEO may authorize structural modifications to this architecture. Agents may recommend changes but may never modify this document autonomously.

This document defines the current validated architecture of Corbenn Labs. It should evolve only through validated operational experience, never through speculation. Corbenn Labs prioritizes execution over documentation and automation over repetitive manual work.
json.approved_research:
# RESEARCH SUMMARY
The objective was to identify recent YouTube Shorts trends that independent music artists can learn from. Evidence was gathered from YouTube official artist resources, YouTube trend reports, and recent YouTube independent-artist examples.

---
# KEY FINDINGS

1. Finding: Low-production selfie performance, teasers, and behind the song Shorts are proven artist formats. YouTube's own artist guide says selfie performance videos are the most common successful Shorts strategy for artists, and high-production video is not critical. Examples listed by YouTube include Tom Odell teasing unreleased music, SEB explaining song meaning, and JAX telling the story behind Victoria's Secret.
Why it matters: Independent artists can compete without expensive visuals if the Short creates intimacy, context, or repeatable emotion.
Confidence: High

2. Finding: Fan participation is a major driver: dance challenges, remixes, captions, slowed/sped versions, and creator reinterpretations expand songs beyond the artist's own audience. Ana Laura Lopes' Fantasma went viral on Shorts with over 400K creations, spawning dance challenges and driving millions of streams/views.
Why it matters: The Short should not only showcase the song; it should invite others to use it.
Confidence: High

3. Finding: Shorts work best when connected to a wider YouTube ecosystem: official audio, long-form videos, release cycles, and analytics. YouTube says Shorts featuring an artist's music tripled average artist reach in January 2024, and artists posting Shorts weekly saw more than 60% of new subscribers come from Shorts.
Why it matters: For independent artists, Shorts are not just viral clips; they can become a discovery-to-subscriber pipeline.
Confidence: High

---
# ACTIONABLE IDEAS

Title: Raw Chorus Test
Hook: I wrote this chorus for anyone who pretends they're fine.
Why this idea matches the evidence: Selfie performance and emotional context are supported by YouTube's artist guidance.

Title: Fan Creation Prompt
Hook: Use this sound for the moment you finally let go.
Why this idea matches the evidence: Ana Laura Lopes' example shows that fan creations and dance/challenge formats can multiply reach.

Title: Behind-the-Line Short
Hook: This lyric sounds simple, but it came from the worst night of the year.
Why this idea matches the evidence: YouTube highlights behind the song storytelling as an artist Shorts format, and it adds meaning before asking for streams.

---
# RISKS

- The strongest evidence comes from platform-level guidance and examples, not Oskar-specific analytics.
- Viral Shorts performance is inconsistent; YouTube notes Shorts view counts can vary widely even on the same channel.
- Some examples are major or established artists, so independent artists should test formats, not copy outcomes.

---
# NEXT STEP
Marketing Strategist - the evidence is ready to be translated into a testable Shorts growth strategy for Oskar Corbenn.
